editorial.headline: International Trade Finance: Open Nationally, Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: International trade finance permits up to 100% foreign ownership nationally, yet foreign investors cannot register this activity at a Bali address under the island-wide PMA moratorium.
editorial.body:
For a foreign investor, the Bali answer is unambiguous: this activity cannot be registered there today through a foreign-investment (PMA) vehicle. That result does not recast the activity itself; it reflects Bali’s island-wide, permanent PMA moratorium for Low and Medium-Low risk activities. The record identifies the Besar form of this activity as Low risk, so the moratorium blocks a PMA registration using a Bali address. The decisive distinction is geographical: the national position is open, while Bali prevents the foreign-investment registration.

At its centre, this is international trade finance: providing financial support, often with additional services, to help entities send goods to and receive goods from around the world. It concentrates on the financial underpinning of international goods flows. The stated scope expressly includes Indonesia’s export-financing institution, giving the category a clear institutional reference as well as its wider commercial purpose. The relevant activity is therefore the support that enables cross-border trade, including accompanying services where they are combined with that financial support. It should be read as a scope for a provider of that support, rather than as a description of the goods-moving operation itself.

Nationally, the activity is TERBUKA—open to PMA—with a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling. A foreign investor may therefore hold the full permitted interest at the national level. The entry is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, placing the stated scope within the record’s full range of business sizes rather than confining it to one tier. Those scales answer the question of who can register by size: a business operating at any of the four listed scales. Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021 is the record’s cited national source for that open status and ownership ceiling.

Bali changes the conclusion without changing those national facts. The provincial rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk activities from PMA registration, island-wide and permanently. For this activity, the record ties the block to the Besar scale’s Low-risk designation and cites gubernatorial letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP, issued in May 2026. The operative Bali fact is the block, not an alternative local ownership ceiling. At a Bali address, the PMA route is closed for this activity, even though the national framework otherwise permits up to 100% foreign ownership.
